summary: Write the feature guide page for three product areas with the cheap model and with the mid model, to choose which one writes the rest

guide.what_it_is_for: The composer is the box at the bottom of a chat where a person types, pastes, attaches and sends a message. It must feel like the leading chat products: type, press Enter, get an answer, and never lose what was typed. This area covers typing, sending, stopping, queuing a next message, drafts that survive reloads, pasting long text or code, and the small controls that add context (mentions, slash commands, chips, voice).
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person who opens a chat on Web, Desktop (which shows the hosted web app), Mobile, the terminal CLI, the VS Code extension and the Chrome extension side panel. Some controls are plan- or capability-gated in code (for example deep research and cloud code execution check useCapabilityDecision and useCapability in ChatComposerNew.tsx:1603-1660, and free-trial users have research switched off at ChatComposerNew.tsx:2187-2216). Developers reach the same code to change behaviour. Nothing in this area is limited to workspace admins as far as the code I opened shows.

features.name: Type and send a message
features.use: The core loop: write text, press the send button or Enter, and stop a reply that is still being written. A character counter warns when the message is near its length limit.
how_people_use_it: Click into the box and type. Line breaks are kept.
Press Enter (or tap the send arrow on Mobile) to send. Shift+Enter inserts a new line.
While a reply is streaming, the send control becomes a stop control (titled Stop generation); click it to end the reply and keep what was produced.
Watch the counter under the box once the text passes 75% of the limit.
how_it_should_work: Empty box: send does nothing. The send button shows a reason when it cannot send (SendButton.tsx:79 uses a disabledReason or an empty-box reason).
Offline: sending is blocked with a notice and the text stays in the box (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3574-3590).
Secret-looking text (an API key pattern): the first send shows a warning and does not send; sending again goes through (ChatComposerNew.tsx:3652-3660).
Counter: shown from 75% of the limit (ChatComposerNew.tsx:296), shows an exceeded state at the limit (ChatComposerNew.tsx:4762), and the input has a hard maxLength (ChatComposerNew.tsx:5898).
Stop keeps the partial reply. Failure to send restores the text into the box with a notice (see the drafts feature).
Plan limits: the length limit comes from a shared cloud-contract constant; its value was not read.

features.name: Keyboard send keys and undo
features.use: Choose whether Enter sends or adds a line, insert a new line with Shift+Enter, and undo or redo edits in the box.
how_people_use_it: Open Settings > General and switch Send with Enter on or off (web settings).
With the setting off, press Enter to add a new line and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter to send.
Press Shift+Enter for a new line in any mode.
Press Cmd/Ctrl+Z to undo and Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z to redo in the editor.
how_it_should_work: Default: Enter sends (web-settings-store.ts:133 sets sendWithEnter to true).
Enter is ignored while an @ or slash menu owns the key, and during IME composition (CJK candidate selection) (ChatComposerNew.tsx:4654-4663).
Cmd/Ctrl+Enter always sends, even with Enter set to newline.
Undo and redo come from the editor's history extension (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/composer-editor/extensions/index.ts:25).

features.name: Growing and expandable box
features.use: The box grows as text is typed, up to a cap, and can be made taller by hand or opened full screen so a long prompt is easier to read and edit.
how_people_use_it: Type; the box grows line by line.
Scroll inside the box when the cap is reached.
Click the expand control (label Expand message input / Collapse message input, ChatComposerNew.tsx:4722-4724) to enlarge it.
On Mobile, use the expand action to open the full-screen editor (ChatInput.tsx:1616-1620, ComposerFullScreenEditor.tsx), then return the text to the composer.

Expanded height: min(60% of the viewport height, 40rem) (ComposerInput.tsx:54).
Expanded state resets when the chat changes (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2140 sets it false).
Escape collapses the expanded box when no menu is open (ChatComposerNew.tsx:4670-4680 area).
Full-screen editing returns the edited text to the composer when closed (behaviour from the brief; the return path was not read).

features.name: Paste text, files and code
features.use: Paste text, images or files into the box. Formatted text becomes plain text. Pasted source code is wrapped in a code block. A very long paste becomes a text file attachment instead of filling the box.
how_people_use_it: Paste with Cmd/Ctrl+V. Images and files become attachment chips.
Paste formatted text from a web page; only plain text lands in the box.
Paste source code; it is wrapped in a fenced code block with a language tag. An undo notice lets the person restore the raw paste (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2400-2412 stores pastedCodeUndo).
Paste 10,000 characters or more; it becomes a file named Pasted text.txt (or Pasted text 2.txt and so on).
how_it_should_work: Order of decision: files first, then large text (threshold 10,000 characters, composerPaste.ts:12), then code detection, then plain text (composerPaste.ts:131-142 and ChatComposerNew.tsx:2379-2383).
Code detection: JSON is not wrapped; text already holding a code fence is not wrapped; the line-shape signals must reach at least half the lines (composerPaste.ts:201-223).
On Mobile, when the composed text would pass the limit, the largest pasted blocks are turned into attachments first (ChatInput.tsx:882-886).
Failure: an unsupported file is refused with a notice (the image-mode notices are at ChatComposerNew.tsx:2249-2262).

features.name: Drafts that survive reloads and stay per chat
features.use: Unsent text is saved while typing, comes back after a reload or a failed send, and never moves into another chat.
how_people_use_it: Type, then reload the page or close the app. The text is still there.
Switch to another chat: the draft of the first chat stays with it.
After a failed or blocked send, the text returns to the box with a notice that nothing was sent.
how_it_should_work: Web: the draft is written to browser local storage per conversation (composer-draft-storage.ts:211 writePersistedDraft) and, for a managed-cloud conversation, saved to the server with a revision check (services/conversation-draft.ts:120-165).
Conflict: if the server copy changed on another device, the person chooses between their text and the other copy (use-conversation-draft-sync.ts:346-349 and the conflict controls).
New-chat draft uses a shared key (composer-draft-storage.ts:4, NEW_CHAT_DRAFT_KEY).
A blocked send is parked under its own fingerprint, not a conversation id, and restored on the next mount (ChatComposerNew.tsx:4290-4335).

Failure: a storage that cannot be written is tolerated (writeRecord returns false, composer-draft-storage.ts:33-42 area).

how_people_use_it: Press Up in an empty or unchanged composer to step back through earlier prompts. Press Down to step forward; past the newest entry you get back the text you were typing.

how_it_should_work: Up with a multi-line composer moves inside the text first, then goes to older prompts, and finally scrolls the chat (tui_app.rs:4179-4195).
Down mirrors this (tui_app.rs:4196-4200).
The typed draft is kept while browsing and restored on the way back (prompt_history.rs:66-89).
A failed history read or write is logged, not shown (prompt_history.rs:20-27, 47-55).

features.name: Prompt suggestions

features.name: Queued next message, edit or cancel it, and steer a running task
features.use: Type the next message while a reply is still generating and it sends when the reply finishes. Edit or cancel it first. While an agent is working, send guidance that changes the running task without stopping it. A side question can be asked without changing the main task.

how_it_works.detail: The composer shows one of two editors: a plain text box (the default) or a rich editor. The choice comes from a query value, then a stored value, then a build-time setting. It is read after the page loads so the server and browser render the same thing first.

The web composer reads the Send with Enter setting and handles Enter, Shift+Enter, Cmd/Ctrl+Enter, Escape and Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Enter. The rich editor handles Enter through a separate key extension. Enter is ignored while a menu or IME composition owns it.
Pasted or dropped files become attachments. Large text (10,000 characters or more) becomes a text file. Code is wrapped in a fence. Everything else is inserted as plain text.

A send is refused when the box is empty and there is no attachment, when offline, or when a slash command cannot run. A message that looks like it contains a secret gives one warning before it can go through. A free-model handoff may switch web search on.

Image and video modes are sent to their own generation paths and are not queued. A normal message goes to the chat send handler. Plan and capability checks produce a notice when a feature is not allowed.
While a turn is active the send control becomes Queue message. Queued messages wait in a list. When the turn ends the next one is sent. A queued message can be edited, cancelled or steered.

Each keystroke updates the message state and the draft is written to browser storage under a key for the conversation (or the shared new-chat key). The write is wrapped so a blocked storage does not break typing.

how_it_works.step: 8. Save the draft to the server
how_it_works.detail: For a managed-cloud conversation the draft is also saved to the server after a short delay, one save at a time per conversation, with a revision number. A 409 response opens a conflict choice.

how_it_works.step: 9. Restore after a failed or blocked send
how_it_works.detail: A send that the guard refused is parked and put back into the box on the next mount, or when the parked text arrives while the composer is open. Live typing is never overwritten.
Mobile keeps its own draft store (device storage) and its own input component. The terminal keeps prompt history in a file and moves through it with the Up and Down keys.

guide.what_it_is_for: A routine is a saved instruction (a prompt) that AGI Workforce runs later without the person present. It runs once at a set time, on a repeat, when an outside event arrives (GitHub, Slack, Gmail, Calendar or webhook), or when someone presses Run now. The person gets recurring work done, such as a daily summary, without opening a chat each time. Each run keeps its output and status so the person can check what happened.
guide.who_uses_it: Signed-in account holders on the apps that show the schedules screen (web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome side panel). Plan limits decide how many routines an account may hold, and a zero-limit plan is refused (apps/web/app/api/schedules/route.ts:105-112, 114-120). Workspace admins can gate the feature for a workspace ('schedules' feature gate, route.ts:114). Developers use the CLI (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1073, 1503) and the API (apps/web/app/api/schedules/[id]/runs/route.ts:105; apps/web/public/openapi.json per the brief). Outside services send events through the webhook and trigger endpoints. Runs use the owner's account for usage and budget.

how_it_works.step: Create or edit in the form
how_it_works.detail: The person fills Frequency, prompt, model, access, budget and time zone. The Frequency options are One Time, Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Interval, Custom Cron, Recurrence Rule and When An Event Happens. The form then sends the routine to the schedules API.

The POST handler checks the rate limit and the CSRF token, checks the plan's schedule limit, checks the workspace feature gate, and refuses a prompt with blocked secrets. Then, in one transaction, it takes a per-user advisory lock, re-checks the quota and creates the routine.
The service validates the input (sources, connectors, model, recurrence, time zone, credit cap) and writes the routine row. Lists are paged through listSchedules.

A scheduled call hits the run-schedules route. It checks the cron authorization, skips in low-power mode, then runs waves of up to 10 due runs inside a 55 second budget, stopping when the queue is empty.

how_it_works.step: Claim and run each due routine
how_it_works.detail: The sweep first expires lapsed approvals and recovers expired claims. It then claims due routines with a lease, and runs each claimed one with a concurrency cap, using a user-scoped database connection.

The executor builds the tool plan from the routine's sources and connectors, chooses a route, and runs a tool loop. A tool that needs approval pauses the run, and the run continues after the owner approves.
The result or error is written to the run row, the status is set, the next run time is set, and a missed occurrence gets a reason. A reached credit cap pauses the routine.

An outside event is verified and recorded as a delivery. A job then checks that the trigger is enabled, creates an event-triggered run (replayed if the same event comes again), and adds the event text to the prompt.
A signed webhook POST is checked against the per-trigger secret. Run now and the API call create a manual run with an idempotency key.

guide.what_it_is_for: This area lets a person see their plan, compare plans, pay for an upgrade, change or cancel a plan, and find their invoices, receipts and refunds. It matters because money is taken here, so the screens must say clearly what will be charged, when, and how to undo or fix it. Most of the work runs on the web app: Stripe (the outside payment provider) holds the card, the invoices and the tax details, and our server asks Stripe and stores only the Stripe ids. The mobile app shows the same plan and can take store (Apple or Google) purchases, but its in-app purchase switch is off in this version.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user who sees the Settings > Billing page or the upgrade pages. Free users see the upgrade path. Paid users see plan, status, invoices and cancel or resume. Team owners and workspace admins see seats and enterprise contract details (code: apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceBillingSummary.tsx:110-135, and apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceEnterpriseContract.tsx:278). Buying a first paid plan is blocked for most accounts until an upgrade gate is open or an access code is redeemed (apps/web/lib/server/billing-waitlist-access.ts:42-54). Accounts scheduled for deletion or with an open dispute cannot buy or change a plan (apps/web/lib/services/billing-plan-change-gate.ts:44-68).

features.name: Buy a paid plan (checkout) and see the result
features.use: Lets a signed-in user start a paid plan through a hosted Stripe checkout page, see the trial terms before paying, and see a confirmation once the plan is active.
how_people_use_it: Choose a plan on the pricing or upgrade page and press the plan button.
The web app sends the request to the checkout endpoint and is sent to the hosted Stripe checkout page.
Read the trial disclosure on the checkout page if the plan has a free trial, then enter payment details and accept the terms.
After paying, Stripe sends the person back to /billing?success=true; the app waits for the plan to show as active (polls for up to 30 seconds) and then shows the confirmation.
how_it_should_work: Only a signed-in user can start checkout; the request must carry the CSRF token and an idempotency key so a double-click does not create two checkouts.
If the account already holds a live paid subscription, checkout refuses and points to Billing to manage it (no second subscription).
If the account has no live paid subscription and no waitlist access, the server returns 403 with the waitlist message (paid upgrades open in stages).
Trial terms (length, end date, amount after the trial, how to cancel) appear on the checkout page and are built from the trial length and the price.

Failure: a Stripe card error shows its message; an unknown configuration error asks the person to contact support; a payment-provider outage asks the person to retry. Nothing is created when the billing state cannot be verified.
Confirmation: the page shows what was bought and that it is active once the subscription row shows the new plan as active or trialing.

features.name: Tax, total and billing details
features.use: Shows tax and the total before a person pays, collects the billing address, and lets a business enter a tax ID (VAT, GST) that is applied to its invoices.
how_people_use_it: Read the order panel or the Order details list before paying; the tax line and the total are shown.
On the hosted checkout page, enter the full billing address (required).
If buying as a business, enter the tax ID in the tax ID field offered by the checkout page; it is validated by Stripe.
how_it_should_work: Tax is calculated by the payment provider from the buyer's location. Prices in the USD are tax-exclusive (tax added on top); INR prices already include tax.
The full billing address is required so tax invoices are valid.
The tax ID is collected by the provider and stored on the provider's customer record, not in our database.
Failure: if tax cannot be calculated the checkout result is marked and the webhook must not silently provision (described in code; webhook not read).
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Desktop: done. Mobile: partial; the tax and total shown are those of the store and of the web checkout; the in-app purchase switch is off.

features.name: Downgrade review and scheduled plan change
features.use: Before a person moves to a smaller plan, shows what changes (price, features, limits, date) and asks them to confirm. The change is scheduled for the end of the current period.
how_people_use_it: On Settings > Billing press Switch to a smaller plan.
The review dialog loads the plan options and shows the current plan, the target plan and the effective date.
Choose a target plan, read the from-to rows (feature and limit changes), then press Confirm to schedule the change.
To switch a yearly plan to monthly, press the cadence switch button and confirm in the dialog that opens.
how_it_should_work: Loads the plan change state first; while loading it says it is checking the plan.
If the change is blocked it explains why: a pending cancellation (resume first), a team or enterprise plan (change in Manage billing), or the smallest paid plan (cancel instead).
On failure it says the plan change could not be scheduled and nothing was changed.
Closing the dialog during submission is not allowed.
features.on_each_app: Web: done (dialog). Desktop: done (same dialog). Mobile: not done; mobile sends plan changes to the store or to web billing and has no downgrade review.

features.name: Cancel, resume and end-of-term access
features.use: Lets a person cancel a plan at the end of the period, resume it before the end, see the cancel date, and understand what they keep until then.
how_people_use_it: On Settings > Billing press Cancel plan. The app opens the Stripe billing portal straight on the cancel step.
After a cancel is scheduled, the Billing page shows a notice with the end date and a Resume button (Resume Plan or Continue after the trial).
Press Resume to keep the plan; the page refreshes with the new state.
how_it_should_work: Cancel is available only for a paid, web-billed plan that is not already ending; it is not offered for store-billed plans.
The notice says the plan ends on a date, that features and credits stay until then, and that the account then moves to Free; chats, projects and files stay.
Resume needs an idempotency key and asks the payment provider to keep the plan; nothing changes if it fails.
If the portal has cancellation turned off, the server answers 409 with a message to open Manage billing or contact support.
Limit: a plan cannot be resumed after it has already ended.
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Desktop: done. Mobile: partial; shows the cancel date and sends the person to the store or to web billing; it has no resume action. VS Code: shows the scheduled cancellation with its date. CLI and Chrome: not applicable in the brief.

features.name: Payment method
features.use: Lets a person see the card or other method that will be charged, mark the default, and add or change one.
how_people_use_it: Open Settings > Billing and read the saved payment method rows (brand, last four digits, expiry, default mark).
To add or update a method, press Update payment method (opens the Stripe billing portal) or complete a new checkout.
how_it_should_work: The list shows every type of method, not only cards (for example Link).
The default is the one the subscription is charged on; if the subscription has its own default, that one wins.
Failure: if the list cannot load, the section shows Payment methods could not be loaded.
Removal is done in the billing portal; no delete button exists in the web Billing section (not verified).
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Desktop: done. Mobile: not listed as a feature in the brief; mobile shows Managed on the web or no payment row.

features.name: Payment failure and retry
features.use: Tells a person clearly when a renewal or a checkout payment fails, and gives a way to fix it: pay the open invoice or update the card.
how_people_use_it: When a renewal fails, Settings > Billing shows a red notice: Your last plan payment didn't go through; press Pay amount now (opens the open invoice) or Update payment method (opens the billing portal).
The payment failure help page (linked from the notice) explains why a payment fails and what to do.
In the CLI, VS Code and Chrome side panel, a warning line tells the person the last payment did not go through and points to Settings > Billing.
how_it_should_work: Past-due and unpaid plans show the notice; enterprise plans do not get this notice.
The notice says paid features stop at the first failed renewal and return when the payment succeeds; chats and files stay.
Checkout failures (card declined, 3D Secure closed) are explained on the payment-failure page; no subscription is created and no charge is made.
Failure of the retry itself is handled by the provider's own pages.
features.on_each_app: Web: done (notice and payment-failure page). Desktop: done. Mobile: done (cloud billing screen shows the warning). CLI: done (usage summary line). VS Code: done (command setup text). Chrome: done (side panel text).

features.name: Invoices, receipts and refunds
features.use: Lets a person see past bills, download invoice PDFs and receipts, and see the status of refunds. Credit notes are not shown anywhere.
how_people_use_it: Open Settings > Billing and scroll to the invoice list; press a row link to open the invoice (PDF link or hosted invoice page).
Read the Receipts table; press View receipt to open the receipt for each payment, including credit purchases.
Read the Refunds table (only shown when a refund exists) with requested date, what it was for, amount and status.
how_it_should_work: Invoices and receipts are read from the payment provider on demand; only ids are stored in our database.
Each list is limited (a page of 24 invoices; receipts and refunds are read from the same payment history).
Empty state: No credit purchases yet. Each one you make gets a receipt here; Not issued yet when a receipt has no link.
Failure: a message such as Invoices could not be loaded or Your refunds could not be loaded, with a retry on refresh.
Credit notes: no code exists for them; the status is missing on every app.
Refund status values: requested, processing, refunded (shown with labels).
features.on_each_app: Web: done (Billing section and the /billing/invoices page). Desktop: done. Mobile: partial; invoices and receipts open on the web, store receipts go to the store, and refund status is not shown (store refunds are handled by the store). Credit notes: missing on all apps.

features.name: Credit purchase and automatic reload history
features.use: Shows the list of credit purchases and their receipts, and the ledger of credit used. Automatic reload is a separate panel; its history is not shown as a list.
how_people_use_it: Open Settings > Billing and find the credit purchases section (or the usage section for the ledger).
Read each row: date, credits, amount and receipt link. Automatic reloads are marked on the row.
how_it_should_work: The credit ledger excludes internal bookkeeping (renewal allocation and reset rows) and never shows which host served a request; the model name is shown.
Empty state: No credit purchases yet.
Failure: Your credit purchases could not be loaded.
A dedicated automatic reload history list does not exist; only a flag on the receipt row shows an automatic reload.
features.on_each_app: Web: done for credit purchases; auto-reload history missing. Desktop: done for credit purchases; auto-reload history missing. Mobile: partial; the mobile app does not call the credit history endpoint, so credit purchases are not shown there.

features.name: Store-billed subscriptions and owner check (mobile)
features.use: For a subscription bought through Apple or Google, tells the person to manage it in that store, warns before a second purchase that would double-bill, and lets them restore a store purchase without being charged again.
how_people_use_it: On the cloud billing screen, read Billed through (for example Managed where you subscribed) and press Manage in the store link when shown.
Press Restore purchases (in the mobile purchase flow) to re-send a store receipt; if a purchase is still waiting, the app asks before buying again.
If a second purchase would double-bill, the app shows the alert Subscription managed elsewhere and offers to open the store.
how_it_should_work: Who owns the subscription is decided by the stored source (web, Apple, Google, organization or none) and by the status.
A store-billed subscription can only be changed in its store; web billing links are hidden where the store forbids them.
Restore sends the store receipt to the server; if verification is not yet done, the app says it has not been discarded and to try Restore shortly.
Failure: a portal open error shows the portal error title with a retry message.
features.on_each_app: Web: done (the web billing section shows the owner and blocks a second checkout). Desktop: done. Mobile: partial; the owner check and the store links are done, and the restore and purchase code is built, but the in-app purchase switch is off (FEATURES.billing is false and MOBILE_IAP_ENABLED must be set on the server).

features.name: Team seats and enterprise billing
features.use: Lets a team owner buy seats (choose a seat count and a seat type), lets an admin see seats used against seats licensed, and lets an enterprise record its billing and procurement contacts and pay by purchase order or invoice.
how_people_use_it: On the team plan card, pick the seat count and seat type (standard or premium) and press the buy button; the seat total is shown before checkout.
In the workspace console, admins read Plan and seats (plan, seats used of the maximum, members) and can invite members to take seats.
Enterprise admins open the contract section to see and record billing and procurement contacts and the PO and invoice terms.
how_it_should_work: Seat count must be valid for the plan; premium seats must exist for the chosen interval and currency, otherwise checkout refuses with a message to choose standard seats.
A first team purchase is blocked by the upgrade gate (403) until access is granted; seat increases are done in the app through the upgrade route.
Seats used are shown as used of maximum; if the maximum is unknown only the member count is shown.
Enterprise contacts are stored in the contract store; invoices carry PO numbers and terms.
Failure: the enterprise contract page shows its own error state.
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Desktop: partial; the team purchase needs a redeemed access code while the billing waitlist is on. API: POST checkout accepts a seat count; seat increases are available only through the app route.

how_it_works.step: 1. The person opens the billing screen or the pricing page
how_it_works.detail: The Settings > Billing section is one React component. It reads the subscription from a shared store and loads plan change state, payment methods, invoices and credit history with separate calls. Plan choice and cadence are on the pricing page.

how_it_works.step: 2. The browser asks the server to start checkout or open the portal
how_it_works.detail: The client helper sends a POST to the checkout endpoint with a bearer token, a CSRF token and an idempotency key. Opening the billing portal posts to the portal endpoint with an optional cancel flow flag. The browser is then sent to the returned Stripe URL.

how_it_works.step: 3. The checkout endpoint checks who may pay
how_it_works.detail: It validates the body, resolves the price for the plan, cadence and country, and checks for an existing live subscription. A waitlist gate returns 403 for accounts without access. The owner policy must allow a new Stripe checkout. The stored Stripe customer is re-checked live with Stripe so a second subscription cannot be started.

how_it_works.step: 4. The checkout session is created with tax, trial and terms
how_it_works.detail: The session is created in subscription mode with tax calculation, tax ID collection, full billing address, promotion codes enabled, the trial terms and the withdrawal consent text. Older open checkouts for the same user are expired.

how_it_works.step: 5. Mid-cycle upgrades use a preview token and a live price check
how_it_works.detail: An existing subscriber upgrades through the upgrade endpoint. It re-reads the live Stripe price, refuses anything that is not an upgrade, verifies the signed preview token, applies the promotion, and then changes the subscription with proration.

how_it_works.step: 6. Cancel, resume and the billing portal go to Stripe
how_it_works.detail: Cancel opens the Stripe portal on its cancel step. The portal endpoint checks ownership, looks up the Stripe customer (stored id first), and creates a portal session. Resume calls a separate endpoint that keeps the current plan in Stripe and then updates the stored cancellation flag.

how_it_works.step: 7. Read-side endpoints fetch from Stripe on demand
how_it_works.detail: Payment methods, invoices, receipts and refunds are read live from Stripe for the stored customer. Credit purchase history is read from our own ledger table and projected so that internal routing details are not returned.

how_it_works.step: 8. Stripe tells the server the result; the page waits for it
how_it_works.detail: The checkout success page returns to /billing. The purchase-confirmation component keeps refreshing the user for up to 30 seconds until the stored plan matches and is active or trialing, then shows the confirmation. The actual state change comes through the payment webhook, which was not opened.

how_it_works.step: 9. Notices and the owner decision are derived from the stored row
how_it_works.detail: The stored subscription row decides the owner (web, Apple, Google, organization or none), whether the portal may open and whether a checkout may start. The notices (past due, trial, ending) are built from the plan change state.

how_it_works.step: 10. Mobile reads the same state and decides what it may show
how_it_works.detail: The mobile cloud billing screen derives its rows from the subscription source and status. Management links are chosen by a pure function. Portal calls are blocked while the billing flag is off. Store purchase and restore state sit in a separate hook.

key_files.role: The Settings > Billing screen: plan card, cancel and downgrade buttons, payment methods, invoices, credit purchases, overage toggle.
Starts a paid checkout: validates the plan, checks waitlist and owner rules, creates the Stripe customer and checkout session.
Mid-cycle upgrade of an existing subscription with a preview token and proration.
Creates a Stripe billing portal session for manage, update card and cancel.
Browser client functions: fetch payment methods, open the portal, start checkout, handoff to the hosted page.
Decides who owns a subscription (web, Apple, Google, organization, none) and what actions are allowed.
The single place that sets tax parameters for checkout and explains the tax policy.
The paid-upgrade gate: operator flag, env override, or a redeemed access code.
Upgrade preview and confirm dialog with order details, promotion code and trial text.
Notices for past due, trial and ending plans, with pay, update card and resume actions.
The mobile Subscription screen: plan summary, billing source, store purchase and management rows.
Mobile rules that decide the owner guard and where Manage billing goes.
Mobile feature switches; billing is false in this version.
Builds the store product catalog from server configuration; the in-app purchase on/off switch lives here.

switches.effect: When set to 1, paid upgrades are open to everyone, whatever the run-time flag says.

switches.effect: When on, paid checkout, portal and store purchases open to every signed-in account; when off, new upgrades need a redeemed access code.

switches.effect: Map internal product keys to the store product ids for Apple and Google.

switches.name: MOBILE_IAP_GOOGLE_REPLACEMENT_MODES_JSON
switches.effect: Sets how a Google plan change replaces the old one for upgrade and downgrade. Downgrade waits for renewal unless set otherwise.

switches.name: Rate limits

guide.what_it_is_for: The composer is the box where a person types, pastes, dictates and sends a message. It also holds the "+" menu, the "/" command menu, the "@" mention menu, the chips for what is attached, the queue of follow-up messages, and the unsent draft. If it works well, a person never loses text, never sends by accident, and can add context quickly. It is the first thing every user touches in every app.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user of every app. Some parts depend on plan or setup. Dictation can be switched off by a billing flag and a setting. Folder mentions on the web code only show when a desktop host exists. Draft saving to the server only applies to Cloud chats that are not temporary and not on a local model. Free-plan users get a handover to Auto when they pick tools a free model cannot use. A "usage block" or exhausted trial disables the whole composer.

features.name: Typing, new lines and height
features.use: Type a message, add line breaks, and see the box grow as the text grows.
how_people_use_it: Click the box and type.
Press Shift+Enter (web, extension, VS Code) or Shift+Enter / Alt+Enter (CLI) for a new line.
On mobile, the keyboard Return key adds a line and the Send button sends.
Keep typing: the box grows, then scrolls.
how_it_should_work: Line breaks are kept in the sent message.
Web: the box grows to 240px, then scrolls (ComposerInput.tsx:53). Mobile: it grows to 6 lines (apps/mobile/lib/constants.ts:25).
Text is capped at 100,000 characters on the web (cloud message limit), enforced by maxLength on the textarea and by the rich editor.
While an input method (for example Chinese or Japanese candidates) is composing, Enter must not send.
The box lines up right-to-left for Arabic or Hebrew text (dir=auto).
features.on_each_app: Web and Desktop (Desktop shows the hosted web app): done. Mobile: done, TextInput with Return key adding lines. CLI: done in the terminal composer. VS Code and Chrome extension: done in their own side panels. The web has two input types: a plain textarea (default) and a rich editor, chosen by a gate (see switches).

features.name: Send and Stop buttons
features.use: A visible button sends the message. While a reply is running, the same slot becomes Stop.
how_people_use_it: Click or tap the arrow to send.
While a reply streams, click the stop square to end it.
Press Escape in the web composer to stop when no menu is open.
how_it_should_work: The button shows Stop while a turn is active, otherwise Send.
Send is disabled, with a reason shown, when offline, or an attachment conflicts with the chosen model or tools, or the chosen media model is unavailable, or the daily search allowance blocks it.
When the box is empty and voice is available, the slot shows a voice-entry button instead of Send.
Stop keeps what was already produced.
A message that looks like it holds an API key or password is held back once with a warning; send again to continue.
features.on_each_app: All six apps have both. Web: SendButton in ChatComposerNew.tsx:6958, handleStop calls onStop supplied by WebChatPage. Mobile: ChatInput has a send state of idle, streaming or queued. CLI: Esc or Ctrl-C cancels a running reply and keeps what streamed.

features.name: Enter key choice and shortcuts
features.use: Choose whether Enter sends or adds a line, and use normal undo and redo.
how_people_use_it: Web Settings > General > Send with Enter: turn it off so Enter adds a line and Cmd/Ctrl+Enter sends.
VS Code setting agiWorkforce.composer.enterBehavior: enter, modifierIfMultiline or modifier.
Cmd/Ctrl+Z undoes, Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z redoes (web, browser-native in textarea; undo extension in the rich editor).
CLI: Ctrl+_ undoes, Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes, Ctrl+E or Ctrl+G opens your external editor.
how_it_should_work: The choice is remembered and the web value syncs with the account's settings.
Cmd/Ctrl+Enter always sends even when Enter-to-send is off.
Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Enter sends the other way (steer instead of queue, or the reverse) while a reply runs.
features.on_each_app: The brief lists Enter-to-send as missing on every app, but the code shows it exists on the web (and so on Desktop) and in VS Code. See things_that_look_wrong. Mobile, CLI and Chrome: no setting found. Undo: web and desktop done (browser or editor undo extension); CLI has its own undo stack; mobile and VS Code rely on the platform text input (unverified); Chrome uses the browser's textarea undo, with helper code that inserts text through execCommand so undo still works (composerText.ts).

features.name: Manual expand and full-screen editing
features.use: Make the box bigger than its automatic height, or edit a long draft in a larger editor.
how_people_use_it: Web: click the expand arrows at the top-right of the box (shown once the text is taller than a threshold). Click again or press Escape to collapse.
Mobile: tap the expand glyph at the top-right of the card to open a full-screen editor; tap Collapse editor to return.
CLI: press Ctrl+E or Ctrl+G to edit the draft in your editor (VISUAL or EDITOR, else vi).
how_it_should_work: Expanded height is the smaller of 60% of the screen height or 40rem on the web.
The text is kept when you return to the composer.
The expand control only shows when there is something to expand.
Changing chat collapses it.
features.on_each_app: Web and Desktop: expand done (the web expand box is the full-screen-like editor). Mobile: full-screen modal (ComposerFullScreenEditor) with its own send button. CLI: external editor only, no resize. VS Code and Chrome: no expand control.

features.name: Paste handling
features.use: Paste text, rich text, files, images and code in a sensible way, and do not let huge pastes flood the box.
how_people_use_it: Paste with Cmd/Ctrl+V.
Paste a file or image: it becomes an attachment.
Paste code: it is wrapped in a code block, with an undo link to paste it as plain text.
Paste a very long text: it becomes a file named Pasted text.txt.

how_it_works.detail: The chat page renders the composer in two places (new chat and open chat) and hands it the send, stop, steer and voice callbacks.

A gate chooses the plain textarea (default) or the rich editor, from a build setting, then a stored override, then a URL parameter. The rich editor adds undo, mentions, a length limit and Enter handling.
The key handler first gives keys to the slash menu and mention menu, then handles Arrow Up to edit the last message, shortcuts, the Enter rule and Escape. An effect resizes the box up to a ceiling.
One shared function decides: files become attachments, text of 10,000 characters or more becomes a text file, code gets fenced, otherwise the paste lands as text.

The / menu uses built-in plus custom commands from the settings store. The @ menu merges skills, projects, connectors, desktop folders and library files. The + menu holds attach, tools and Output rows.

handleSubmit builds the send arguments (text, files, skill, tool options, output format). If a reply is running it creates a queued item; otherwise it calls onSend. Unsent text is cleared only after a send is accepted.
When the running reply ends, the first queued item for this chat is sent; items for another chat are turned into drafts. Steer sends text to the running cloud task instead.
As the text changes it is written to browser storage under a key made from the owner id and chat id, and cleared for temporary chats.

After a delay a hook sends a PUT with the draft to the conversation, with the last revision so a clash from another device returns 409 and opens a keep-mine or keep-theirs choice. The server stores it on the conversation row.
Mobile, CLI and the two extensions each have their own composer code that uses the same ideas (shared paste thresholds on mobile and Chrome).

guide.what_it_is_for: A routine is a saved prompt that the Cloud runs for you without you being present. It can run once, on a repeating clock, when an outside event arrives (GitHub, Slack, Gmail, Calendar, a signed webhook), or when you press Run now. You get the result in a run history, and the run stops and asks you when it needs approval for a risky step. It saves repeat work (briefings, inbox triage, monitoring) and keeps cost bounded through run limits and credit caps.
guide.who_uses_it: Signed-in users on a plan that includes scheduled tasks. The cap is read from the plan table: local-only, own-key (byok) and Free get 0 (so the create call is refused with an upgrade prompt), Basic 3, Pro 5, Max 15, a plan named max_15x 25, Team 10, Enterprise 'custom' (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:593-723). Routines are Cloud-only: they run on the server, not on the device. Workspace members must still be active members of their workspace for runs to fire, and the access gate can block them (apps/web/app/api/schedules/route.ts:96-103). The only Local-mode path is the Desktop "local routines" panel on web (LocalRoutinesSection.tsx), which runs through the desktop host bridge.

Name and description editable on every app that edits routines.

Time zone is validated. An invalid one is refused.

Cadence is checked for deliverability: the cloud wakes every 15 minutes (vercel.json:50, SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS), so faster schedules are refused or run late (assertDeliverableCadence). Mobile shows a note about this.
Retries: 0 to 5, first wait 1 minute to 1 day, doubling (retryDelaySeconds).
A routine that gets an expiry date must still have a first occurrence before it.
Mobile supports only once, daily, weekly, monthly; interval or cron creation throws an error telling the user to use Web (policy.ts:4-8, 40-45).

features.name: Event triggers and webhooks
features.use: Start a routine when something happens outside: a GitHub event, a Slack message, a new Gmail email, a Calendar change, or a signed POST to a URL the routine owns. A documented API call can also start a run.
how_people_use_it: Open a routine, then the Triggers panel (web/desktop), the Triggers screen (mobile) or agi schedules triggers add (CLI).
Choose source (GitHub, Slack, Gmail, Google Calendar, or 'Anything else (signed webhook)').
Fill the account (repository, Slack team id, mailbox) and optionally event types.
Optionally add field conditions (narrow by data) and a repeat-suppression wait.
Save. For a webhook the screen shows a URL and a signing secret once. For Slack it shows a verification code to post in the workspace.
Gmail: press Register watch if the mailbox watch fails.
Regenerate the signing secret from the trigger row (asks first).
how_it_should_work: The webhook URL accepts POSTs of up to 128 KB that carry headers x-agi-timestamp and x-agi-signature (sha256 HMAC of timestamp.body). A bad or old signature returns 401. A missing server key returns 503 (webhooks/connectors/[triggerId]/route.ts:46-100).
Body must be a JSON object with an id (delivery id) and a type.
An event only reaches a trigger if its owner holds the source account (GitHub installation, Slack workspace). Up to 20 triggers per event (trigger-ingest.ts:28).
Conditions and a debounce window can filter out events. Each outcome (filtered, debounced, enqueued, duplicate, failed) is recorded.
A matching event is queued as a job; the job fires the run with the event data appended to the prompt as untrusted data (promptWithEventContext).
Event fire limits: 30 per hour and 720 per day (PLATFORM_EVENT_TRIGGER_RUNS_PER_HOUR/DAY).
If the routine is paused or deleted before the job starts, the delivery is marked filtered with the reason.
A routine of type event has no clock time; clock fields, day-parts and a watch condition are refused for it.
API trigger: the runs endpoint is documented in openapi.json at /schedules/{id}/runs and uses bearer auth; a run needs an Idempotency-Key header.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, CLI have triggers and filters. Mobile has a Triggers screen in code (ScheduleTriggersScreen.tsx, triggers/[id].tsx) although the brief says missing. Chrome and VS Code: none. CLI also has a local daemon with cron, webhook and file-watch triggers that is separate from the Cloud triggers (daemon.rs).

features.name: Run now and run results
features.use: Run a routine immediately and read what each run produced, see when the next and last run are, and see the history list.
how_people_use_it: Press Run now on a routine card (web, desktop, mobile, Chrome side panel); VS Code command 'Code: Run Schedule Now'; CLI agi schedules run <name>.
Open History or Runs on a routine to see status and time for each run; open one to read the output.
Web also has a 'latest result' panel and a recent results list.
how_it_should_work: Run now requires an Idempotency-Key header. Sending the same key again returns the same run instead of running twice (schedule-service.ts createOnDemandScheduleRun).
Run now fails with a conflict if the routine is paused, expired or at its run limit, or if its credit cap is reached.
A manual run is waited for up to 40 seconds inside the request (runs/route.ts:80-86). Longer ones end as a timeout status.
Run statuses: running, success, failed, timeout, cancelled, awaiting_approval.
A run's output text is returned as 'output' with the internal reasoning removed (mapScheduleRun).
Next run is the stored next_execution_at; last run is last_executed_at plus the last error. History pages 20 at a time.
While a run is in progress the web list polls only for routines that are due, and only when the tab is visible.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome, VS Code have Run now in code. CLI also has a run command although the brief says missing. Run history list: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code; Chrome in code has a runs view (schedulesSection.ts:924-1130) although the brief says missing.

features.use: Manage an existing routine: pause and resume it, edit it, delete it, or share a copy of it as a link.

how_it_should_work: Resume recomputes the next time. It is refused if the routine finished, expired, hit its run limit, hit its credit cap or has no further occurrence (setScheduleEnabled, schedule-service.ts:1234-1275).
Delete is refused while a run is in progress. Delete removes the routine and its runs permanently (deleteSchedule: a SQL delete; no trash). The web confirms first.
Stop sharing asks first and says the link stops for everyone, but copies already made stay (SchedulesPage.tsx:782-790).
Sharing is blocked by workspace external-sharing rules and by the outbound secret scan.
A share stores a snapshot (name, prompt, timing, model) at an unguessable token; it excludes sources lists beyond allowed metadata keys.
A shared link only works while its owner may run unattended work (getSharedSchedule).
Pause until a chosen date and Duplicate are not built on any app.

features.name: Cost and safety controls: caps, notifications, approvals
features.use: Keep unattended runs safe and affordable: cap the number of runs or credits per routine, choose how to be told about runs, and require a person to approve risky steps.
how_people_use_it: In the form set Maximum Runs and Credit Cap.
Tick the routine notification choices (success, failure, approval, push, email).
When a run needs approval, a card with Approve and Deny appears in the run history. CLI: agi schedules approve or deny.
how_it_should_work: maxExecutions 1 to 1,000,000; creditCap a whole number of credits within a maximum (schedule-service.ts:720-745).
When the credit cap is reached, the next run pauses the routine with reason credit_cap_reached and the user must raise the cap to resume (pauseForCreditCap).
When a run needs approval it stops in the awaiting_approval status, the routine pauses with reason approval_required, and a notification is queued.
Approving resumes the same run from a saved checkpoint. Denying lets it continue without that step.
If no one answers within the approval time limit the run stops and says to resume the schedule (APPROVAL_EXPIRED_MESSAGE).
The tool gate for unattended runs is in tool-call-gate.ts.
features.on_each_app: Budget: Web and Desktop have caps; mobile, CLI, Chrome none (brief). Approvals: all apps can resolve one. Notification settings: web form has a 'Routine notifications' section and desktop local routines have switches; CLI none.

features.name: Missed runs, retries and held runs
features.use: Explain what happened when a run did not happen on time, and handle failures, usage limits and broken connectors.
how_people_use_it: Open the run history; a missed or skipped run shows a note explaining why.
Pick 'If a run is missed' in Advanced: run it late once, or skip it.
how_it_should_work: A run is 'missed' when it starts more than twice the sweep interval late (30 minutes normally; 2 hours in low-power mode, missedExecutionGraceMs).
The policy decides: run_once runs it late, skip records it and gives the run slot back (releaseExecutionSlot). Both write an audit event.
The note text comes from describeScheduleRunTiming in the shared contracts.
Failed or timed-out runs retry with doubling wait up to the chosen retry count.
Held run after the usage allowance resets: not built. Expired connector repair flow: not built.
features.on_each_app: Missed-run note: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code; Chrome none. Allowance hold and connector repair: none.

how_it_works.detail: A form (web ScheduleForm, desktop DesktopCloudSchedules, mobile ScheduleForm, CLI command, Chrome side panel) collects name, prompt, timing, model, sources, connectors, agent, caps, retries, missed policy and notifications. Templates, chat answers, share links and agents only pre-fill this draft.

Every app calls the same /api/schedules endpoints. The server finds the user, applies rate limit and CSRF check, checks the plan quota (Free and own-key get 0) and the workspace feature gate, and refuses prompts with secrets.

validateScheduleInput rejects unknown fields, bad lengths, bad time zones and impossible timing, checks the model against the catalog, and works out the first next_execution_at. createSchedule inserts the row into scheduled_tasks under a per-user lock; options like sources and connectors are stored in the metadata column.

Vercel calls /api/cron/run-schedules every 15 minutes. It claims up to 10 due routines per wave (up to 50 per sweep) and runs them, each with a time limit. Missed-run detection and the condition watch happen when each claim is processed.

A signed webhook (or GitHub, Slack, Gmail, Calendar receiver) is verified, matched to triggers, filtered by conditions and debounce, and queued as a job. The job creates a run with idempotency key eventId:attempt and appends the event data to the prompt as untrusted text.
POST /api/schedules/{id}/runs needs an Idempotency-Key. It creates a running row (or returns the earlier one for the same key) and runs the agent in the same request with a 40-second limit.

The executor re-checks secrets, plan access and agent, picks a route for the model (refusing routes unfit for Google user data or no-training settings), builds the allowed tool list from sources and connectors, and runs the tool loop with approvals set to pause. Result text, tools used and cost are stored.

If a step needs approval the run becomes awaiting_approval with a checkpoint, the routine pauses, and a notification job is queued. The approval endpoint loads the checkpoint and resumes the same run.
Run rows are mapped to a public shape with the output text, status, error and a timing note, and shown in each app's history list.

guide.shared_code: Shared: the server (apps/web/app/api/schedules, schedule-service.ts, scheduled-agent-executor.ts, triggers) is the only place routines live. Types, validation schemas, templates, paths, page-size limits and the missed-run wording are in packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts and used by web, desktop, mobile and the Chrome panel. Plan limits come from packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts. Time helpers (cron builder, local-to-ISO) are in packages/platform/utils/src/scheduling. Separate per app: every UI (web React components, desktop DesktopCloudSchedules.tsx, mobile React Native screens, Chrome DOM side panel, VS Code tree and commands) and the CLI's Rust client. The CLI daemon with local cron, webhook and file triggers and the web LocalRoutinesSection for the Desktop host are separate local mechanisms.

guide.what_it_is_for: This area is where a person chooses a paid plan, pays for it, changes or cancels it, and looks back at what they paid. It also covers credit top-ups, team seats and enterprise contract billing. It matters because it is the only path to paid Cloud plans, and a wrong charge, a missing receipt or a stuck cancellation costs real money and trust.
guide.who_uses_it: Every signed-in user can see plans and Billing. Only Cloud users pay: Local and own-key use need no plan. Paid checkout is currently gated: a user with no live paid plan needs an access code (a row in beta_redemptions) or the operator switch open, otherwise the server answers 403. Team seat and contract screens are for workspace admins with billing permission. Mobile only shows plan status, because in-app purchases are compiled off.

features.name: Compare plans and pick monthly or yearly
features.use: Lets a person see price, usage and features of each plan side by side before choosing, and pick the billing cadence for Team.
how_people_use_it: Open /pricing on web (Desktop shows the same hosted page).
Switch between Individual and Business tabs.
On the Team card click Monthly or Annual in the cadence toggle.
Click the plan button (Upgrade, or Join waitlist when upgrades are gated).
If already on a paid plan, choose Upgrade in the chat upgrade dialog or /upgrade.
On mobile open Settings, Subscription, Compare plans.
how_it_should_work: Prices and the comparison table come from the shared plan catalog and localized prices, not from hardcoded numbers.
The annual toggle appears only when a yearly Team price is ready for the buyer's region; the saving percent is computed from monthly and yearly prices.
Individual plans are always sold monthly; only Team uses the toggle (selectedInterval returns monthly for non-seat plans).
While the account is still loading the button shows 'Checking account...'.
Signed-out users are sent to sign in and come back to /pricing.
If checkout is switched off (STRIPE_CHECKOUT_ENABLED false) or a plan has no price in the region, a toast explains it.
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Desktop: done (the public Desktop shows the hosted web app). Mobile: done as a read-only 'Compare plans' list of what each plan includes; it never sells. CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no comparison screen of their own; VS Code has a Compare plans command that opens the web pricing page.

features.name: Start a paid plan (checkout, access gate, confirmation)
features.use: Takes a signed-in person from a plan button to the hosted payment page and back to a confirmation that the plan is active.
how_people_use_it: Click the plan button on /pricing or /upgrade/<plan>.
If a waitlist dialog appears, enter an access code or join the waitlist.
Get redirected to the hosted payment page, enter card, address and accept terms.
Return to /billing?success=true and wait a few seconds for 'active'.
how_it_should_work: Browser calls POST /api/checkout with plan, billing interval and seats; server refuses a user who already has a live subscription anywhere (store, org or provider) with a clear message.
A user with no live paid plan and no access code gets 403 WAITLIST_ACCESS_REQUIRED, and the page opens the waitlist dialog.
Server builds a subscription checkout session with terms-of-service consent and returns its URL; the browser remembers the session id and plan.
After return, PendingCheckoutConfirmation refreshes the account every 2 seconds for up to 30 seconds and moves to /billing when the plan matches and status is active or trialing.
If the payment service is down, rate limited or rejects the setup, the user sees a plain message and nothing is created.
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Desktop: done (same web page). API: done. Mobile: partial. Purchase, receipt, confirmation and restore code exist but native purchases are compiled off (storePurchases.json nativePurchases false, FEATURES.billing false) and the server needs MOBILE_IAP_ENABLED. CLI/VS Code/Chrome send the user to the web.

features.name: Upgrade a live plan with proration and promotion code
features.use: Lets a paying user move to a higher plan mid-cycle and see exactly what is credited and charged today, with an optional promotion code.
how_people_use_it: On /pricing or /upgrade choose a higher plan.
Read the order details (new plan, credit for unused time, subtotal, discount, tax, total due today).
Optionally click to add a promotion code and apply it.
Click confirm to charge the saved card.
how_it_should_work: The dialog first asks /api/upgrade/preview for a priced preview and a preview token; it shows 'Calculating your prorated cost...' meanwhile.
Each row shown is a real proration line; the note states a new billing period starts today with credit for unused time.
A promotion code is checked server side; a bad or unverifiable code shows an error and the plan stays unchanged.
Confirm calls POST /api/upgrade with the token; the server rejects a stale token and verifies the target price and seat count were applied.
If the current plan has no paid charge to credit, the dialog explains it is not a prorated upgrade and sends the user to checkout.
On failure the message says the current plan is unchanged.
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Desktop: done (same web code). Mobile: shows the proration wording in its billing screen but cannot upgrade in the app. Coupons on first purchase are entered on the hosted payment page (allow_promotion_codes true).

features.name: Tax, billing address and tax ID
features.use: Makes sure the buyer sees tax and a total, can give a full billing address and, for business, a VAT/GST number that goes on invoices.
how_people_use_it: On the hosted payment page type the full billing address.
Tick the business option and enter the tax number.
On mid-cycle upgrades read the Tax row in order details.
On top-ups the same address and tax ID fields appear at payment.
how_it_should_work: Tax is computed by the payment provider's tax engine from the buyer's location; the code keeps no country list.
USD prices are shown without tax and tax is added at checkout; INR prices include tax.
Checkout requires the full billing address and offers tax ID collection; for returning customers the typed address and name are saved for the next renewal.
The product never stores the address or tax ID itself; it reads invoices back from the provider.
The in-app first-purchase screen says 'Tax is calculated at checkout' because the real figure appears on the hosted page.
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Desktop: done. Mobile: partial (store shows its own price and tax; purchase is switched off).

features.name: Trial terms
features.use: When a plan starts with a free trial, tells the person the length, end date, what is charged after and how to cancel.
how_people_use_it: Start checkout on a plan that offers a trial or use a referral that grants one.
Read the note above the pay button on the payment page.
Read the Trialing notice in Settings, Billing, or the mobile billing card ('Free trial ends ..., then renews unless you cancel').
how_it_should_work: Server decides the trial days (plan trial or referral trial); a customer with earlier subscription history gets none.

Text states trial days, end date, the amount plus tax charged on that date and each month or year after, that a reminder email goes out before the end with a one-click cancel link, and that cancel works in Settings, Billing.
Session expires after 1 hour when a trial is offered.
Payment method is always collected; if no method exists at trial end the subscription is cancelled.
If the trial was cancelled, Billing says it will not turn into a paid plan and the account moves to Free.
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Desktop: done. Mobile: done as read-only wording of trial end date.

features.name: Payment methods
features.use: Shows saved cards and lets the person add, change or remove them.
how_people_use_it: Open Settings, Billing, Payment methods.
Read cards (brand, last 4, expiry, Default tag).
Click Add payment method or Manage billing to open the hosted billing portal.
Change default, update or remove the card in the portal.
how_it_should_work: The list is read-only in the product (GET /api/billing/payment-methods) and each card shows Default if it is the default.
Add, update, remove and set default all happen in the provider's hosted portal, opened by POST /api/portal.
Portal is allowed only when the subscription is billed by the web provider; store-billed or org-managed users get a message naming who owns billing.
Empty state offers Add payment method; failure to open shows an error under the buttons.
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Desktop: done. Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not in the brief; VS Code and CLI point to web billing.

features.name: Payment failure and retry
features.use: Tells the person clearly that a payment failed and gives a way to pay the open invoice or update the card.
how_people_use_it: See the red notice at the top of Settings, Billing.
Click 'Pay <amount> now' to open the hosted invoice, or 'Update payment method'.
Read /payment-failure for causes (declined card, 3D Secure closed, network).
In CLI run the usage summary; in VS Code or Chrome open the billing action shown.
how_it_should_work: Status past_due or unpaid shows: last payment didn't go through; paid features stop at the first failed renewal and return when paid; chats and files stay.
Pricing and /upgrade block new upgrades while payment is overdue and point to Billing.
The /payment-failure page also says a failed new checkout created no subscription and no charge.
CLI prints that the account is on Free until settled, with the billing link.
Chrome side panel shows a past-due gate message with a Manage billing action; VS Code lists a 'Manage billing and subscription' item that says 'Restore paid Cloud access on Web'.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: done in their own wording. Retry (S83.15) is web and Desktop only; other apps send the user to web billing.

features.name: Billing history, invoices, receipts, refunds and credit purchases
features.use: Lets a person look back at what they were billed, download proof of payment, follow a refund and see credit activity.
how_people_use_it: Open Settings, Billing or /billing/invoices.
Read the Invoices table; click View or Pay to open the hosted invoice or PDF.
In 'Payment history' click View receipt on a credit purchase; read the refunds table.
Read Credit history for purchases, refunds, bonuses, adjustments and usage debits.
Request a refund through the form on /refund-policy.
how_it_should_work: Invoices come from the payment provider (up to 24, with a Receipt link), credit purchases and refunds from /api/billing/receipts and /api/billing/refunds, credit activity from our credit_transactions table.
Refund status labels come from the provider (Refunded, Partly refunded and similar).
Empty states explain why: store-billed plans say receipts come from the store; free users see 'Invoices appear here once you are billed'.
Failures show an error with Try again.
Credit notes and an automatic-reload history do not exist yet.
features.on_each_app: Web and Desktop: done for invoices, receipts, refunds and credit history. Credit notes (S83.19) and auto-reload history (S83.33): missing on every app. Mobile: only 'View invoices' opens the web, no download, no refund status, and /api/billing/credit-history is never called.

features.name: Cancel, resume, downgrade and end-of-term
features.use: Lets a person cancel at the end of the period, undo it, switch to a smaller plan, and see what they keep until the end.
how_people_use_it: Settings, Billing, click Cancel plan (opens the hosted portal's cancel step).
Click Resume <plan> in the 'ends on' notice to undo.
Click 'Switch to a smaller plan', review the dialog, then confirm.
Click 'Keep <plan>' to undo a scheduled switch.
how_it_should_work: Cancel is end-of-period: the notice says 'Your plan ends on <date>. You keep features and credits until then. After that, your account moves to Free; chats, projects and files stay.'
Resume calls POST /api/billing/resume-cancellation, clears the flags in Stripe, updates cancel_at_period_end in the subscriptions table and returns fresh plan state.

Downgrade dialog loads a preview from /api/billing/downgrade-preview (price, features, limits, date it applies) and the confirm button schedules it; it replaces an earlier scheduled switch and shows a failure message that nothing changed.
Cancel and downgrade buttons show only for web-billed paid plans with no pending change.
features.on_each_app: Web and Desktop: done. Mobile and VS Code: done for showing the cancel date only; mobile has no resume or downgrade review and sends people to the store or web. CLI and Chrome do not show this.

features.name: Store-billed plans, duplicate-subscription warning and purchase restore
features.use: Stops people paying twice and tells those billed by Apple or Google where to manage the plan.
how_people_use_it: Open Settings, Billing and read 'Billed through'.
Click Manage in the App Store or Manage on Google Play.
On mobile tap Upgrade and read the 'Subscription managed elsewhere' alert.
On mobile (when enabled) tap Restore purchases.
how_it_should_work: Billing owner is worked out from ids on the subscriptions row (web provider, Apple, Google, organization); mixed or unreadable ids are 'unverified' and block changes.
Checkout returns 409 with the owner's name if someone already pays elsewhere, and also if the provider already bills a live subscription.
Mobile restore re-checks with the store and never charges again; outcomes: nothing to restore, already restored, store unavailable.
Web links to store management when the plan is store billed.
features.on_each_app: Web, Desktop, Mobile: done for the warning and instructions. Restore: mobile partial, the code is built but the Restore row is hidden because native purchases are compiled off.

features.name: Team seats and enterprise billing
features.use: Lets a team owner buy and assign seats, and lets enterprise admins see contract, contacts, purchase orders and invoice status.
how_people_use_it: On /pricing, Business tab, type seat counts and buy.
Add seats later through the upgrade dialog.
Workspace console shows Plan and seats and the invite flow assigns seats.
Admins read Enterprise contract, Contacts and invoices.
how_it_should_work: Checkout takes seat counts (standard and premium) with a minimum; first Team purchase still needs the access gate.
Seat increases go through POST /api/upgrade, not /api/checkout.
Workspace shows 'Seats used N of M' and the invitation list reports seats.
Enterprise screens are read only and show legal entity, term, cadence, committed seats, payment terms, tax status, purchase order reference and contacts.
Offline payments (wire, check, bank transfer) are recorded against an invoice with a bank reference and cannot be double recorded.
Permission billing.read or billing.contracts.manage is required.
features.on_each_app: Web: done. Desktop: seat purchase partial (waitlist held by owner); contract views done. API: partial (first Team purchase 403 until access). Mobile: seat view done in the workspace screen.

how_it_works.step: Person opens pricing and picks a plan
how_it_works.detail: The pricing page builds cards and the comparison table from the shared plan catalog and localized prices. The Team card holds seat counts and the monthly/annual choice. Clicking a plan runs handleUpgrade.

how_it_works.step: Access gate check in the browser
how_it_works.detail: A user with no paid plan is asked whether upgrades are open to them. If not, the waitlist dialog opens. A user with a live paid plan skips the gate and goes to the upgrade dialog or /upgrade/<plan>.

stripe-payments builds the request with CSRF header and an idempotency key (so a double click cannot make two sessions), posts to /api/checkout, remembers the session id, then hands off to the hosted page.

The route validates the body, picks the price for the buyer's country, reads the subscriptions row, applies the access gate (access code or operator switch), refuses when another owner (store, org) or a live provider subscription exists, and closes older open sessions.

how_it_works.step: Server builds the hosted session with tax, trial and promotion code
how_it_works.detail: It adds trial terms text, terms-of-service consent, promotion codes, the automatic tax and tax ID settings, then returns the session URL and records an audit event.

The success URL is /billing?success=true. PendingCheckoutConfirmation polls the account every 2 seconds for up to 30 seconds and moves to /billing once the plan is active or trialing. The subscriptions table is filled by the provider's webhook.

UpgradeConfirmDialog asks the preview route for a priced order and a token, shows proration and tax, lets the user add a promotion code, then POST /api/upgrade applies the change after checking the token and the result.

how_it_works.step: Billing settings page: status, notices and actions
how_it_works.detail: BillingSection loads plan state, saved cards, invoices and credit history in parallel, derives the billing owner, and shows notices (past due, trial, ending, scheduled change) and buttons (Manage billing, Cancel plan, Switch to a smaller plan, Resume).

how_it_works.step: Portal, resume and downgrade server routes
how_it_works.detail: Cancel, card changes and add payment method open the hosted portal (cancel deep-links to the cancel step when allowed). Resume and downgrade call our routes, which change the subscription at the provider and update subscriptions.cancel_at_period_end.

Invoices, receipts and refunds are read live from the payment provider for the user's customer id; credit history is read from the credit_transactions table. Each list shows loading, empty and error states.
The phone reads plan, status, billing source and period end from /api/me, shows them, and sends web or store billed users to manage elsewhere. Native purchase code is gated by a compile-time value.

Review and confirm a switch to a smaller plan.
Decides who bills a subscription (web, Apple, Google, organization) and what actions are allowed.
Paid-upgrade access gate (access code or operator switch).
The one place that sets tax, address and tax ID collection for checkout.
Mobile Subscription screen: plan status, manage elsewhere, restore, web links.

guide.shared_code: Web, Desktop and the hosted pages are one code base: the Electron Desktop shows the web app, so every web billing screen is also the Desktop screen. Shared packages hold plan prices, plan tiers and capability rules (@agiworkforce/types, imported by pricing, checkout and mobile). Mobile has its own billing store, screens and store-purchase code in apps/mobile/src/features/billing and apps/mobile/src/features/settings. CLI (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs), VS Code (apps/extension-vscode) and Chrome (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts) each have their own small wording for a failed payment and open web billing for the real work.

things_that_look_wrong.what: Brief says S83.33 auto-reload history is missing on every app. AutoReloadPanel has no history list at all (no match for history in the file); only the settings are shown.
Credit notes (S83.19) have no screen or route in the web billing code I searched.
Payment method management is read-only with a Default tag; add, set default, update and remove all go through the hosted portal, not in-product controls as 'Should' reads.
On a first purchase the in-product screen says 'Tax is calculated at checkout', so tax and total are not shown before leaving for the hosted page (they are shown for mid-cycle upgrades).
A user with no access code cannot start any paid checkout, including Team seats; this is an owner decision but contradicts 'a signed-in user can start and complete a paid upgrade'.
Brief line numbers for the CLI, VS Code and Chrome payment-failure entries no longer match: the code is at usage_summary.rs:639, side_panel.ts:13434 and commandSetup.ts:2419.
A failed save of the Stripe customer link after creating the customer is only logged, not shown to the user.
Fallback that finds a customer by email in the portal route is labelled deprecated and a security warning.
Checkout error text for an invalid checkout setup is generic ('Invalid checkout configuration. Please contact support.'), which does not tell the user how to fix it.

How seats are assigned to members beyond invitations and the seat summary (WorkspaceBillingSummary was only partly read), and what the mobile workspace screen shows for seats.
